title: Overlap prefetch + pinned buffer pooling and thread isolation to reduce CPU-GPU churn
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Host-side overhead dominates short-sequence prefill+decode workloads. We observe high CPU utilization from memcpy bursts, frequent blocking on shared threadpool, and repeated DMA handshake on every request which amplifies p95/p99 tails when small batches are common. This ticket experiments with three coordinated mitigations: (1) a pinned-host buffer pool that recycles page-locked buffers to avoid repeated host->device allocation and registration; (2) overlapping DMA-prefetch with prefill tokenization and KV-cache lookups through a per-queue io-fence so copies are decoupled from the critical decode path; (3) a small set of threadpool isolation knobs (dedicated io threads with CPU affinity + an adaptive token-aware queue depth) to reduce contention and priority inversion between prefill and background housekeeping.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p95 latency for small-sequence (<=64 tokens) prefill+decode workloads reduced by >=15% in our lab harness compared to baseline (runtime-1.20)
Host CPU usage attributable to memcpy/host orchestration reduced by >=25% during steady-state QPS=600 test
No regressions in large-batch (>2048 tokens) throughput within 5% of baseline
Implementation behind runtime flag with clear telemetry (per-route memcpy/time breakdowns) and smoke test in CI
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Spike started. Initial microbench harness created that reproduces memcpy bursts with short sequences. Measured host allocation stalls when registering buffers on CUDA driver calls.

2026-02-24 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype pinned buffer pool implemented (single global per-worker pool). Rough numbers: alloc + register erased ~12us per request on warm path; reuse shaved ~9us. Need to handle eviction on memory pressure and NUMA placement.
2026-02-28 - Design review notes (Lydia Chen): Prefer per-GPU per-worker pool to avoid cross-socket penalties. Add soft limit and LRU eviction. Include telemetry for pool hit/miss counts.

2026-03-03 - Marco Ruiz: Added io-fence-based overlap: prefetch copy invoked earlier during tokenization; copy completion checked via non-blocking poll on worker io thread. Observed 18% p95 improvement in artificial harness (QPS=600, seq=32).

2026-03-06 - Notes from infra sync (Diego Alvarez): Threadpool isolation needs extra guardrails for bursty workloads; implement fallback to shared pool if io thread saturated to avoid starvation of background tasks.

2026-03-09 - Benchmark summary (internal): Lab run compared baseline runtime-1.20 vs feature branch: small-seq p95 -18%, p99 -12%; host memcpy CPU slice down ~30%. Large-batch throughput change -1.8% (within target). Planning canary rollout behind feature flag.
2026-03-10 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1728. PR contains pinned buffer pool, io-thread, and telemetry. Requesting reviews from @lydia, @diego, @samir (kernel-selection).
rollout_notes: Feature is hidden behind flag runtime.prefetch_overlap.enabled. Start canary on dedicated pools with 2% traffic for 48 hours. Monitor memcpy_time, io_thread_queue_depth, pool_hit_ratio, and end-to-end latency per-route. If pool_hit_ratio < 80% under expected load, auto-disable and collect heap/profile for investigation.
implementation_summary: Pinned host buffer pool implemented with per-GPU shards, LRU soft eviction, and simple memory-pressure callback. DMA prefetch moved earlier in pipeline and scheduled to a dedicated io thread with CPU affinity. Kernel selection handshake reduced by moving model metadata validation off hot path and caching kernel compatibility per-model/sequence-length bucket. Added telemetry and CI smoke tests.
